claim: TubeArchivist has ~8,067 GitHub stars, only 25 open issues, last release v0.5.10 on 2026-03-28, last code push 2026-05-23 - actively maintained and the most-starred candidate.
PinchFlat has ~5,005 GitHub stars but 211 open issues and its last release (v2025.9.26) and last code push are both from late 2025 - growth-leader but release cadence has stalled.
ytdl-sub has ~2,843 GitHub stars, 122 open issues, and frequent rolling releases (latest 2026.05.10, push 2026-06-04) reflecting active CLI-focused development.
TubeSync has ~2,736 GitHub stars, 59 open issues, and remains actively maintained with a recent v0.18.1 release on 2026-06-02.

On AlternativeTo, TubeArchivist is the top-ranked Pinchflat alternative (5 likes), ahead of TubeSync (1 like) and ytdl-sub, positioning TubeArchivist as the community default and PinchFlat as the simpler challenger.
quote: Tube Archivist is regarded as the best Pinchflat alternative, which is both free and Open Source. Tube Archivist - 5 likes; Tubesync - 1 like; ytdl-sub - No likes indicated.

claim: TubeArchivist's own README states the stack needs ~2GB RAM for a small test setup and ~4GB for mid/large installs, plus a kernel vm.max_map_count tweak for Elasticsearch - the recurring 'heavy' complaint.
quote: the Tube Archivist stack needs around 2GB of available memory for a small testing setup and around 4GB of available memory for a mid to large sized installation.

claim: TubeArchivist's Elasticsearch memory weight is a known long-standing pain point, with users opening issues specifically asking how to make Elasticsearch use less RAM.
quote: How to make elasticsearch use less ram - Issue #102 - tubearchivist/tubearchivist

claim: Reviewers favor PinchFlat as a lightweight single-container alternative because TubeArchivist had 'become too complicated with many features,' and PinchFlat has no external dependencies (no Elasticsearch).
quote: Tube Archivist is noted as having become too complicated with many features and options to navigate, while Pinchflat was sought as a simpler alternative... self-contained with just one Docker container and no external dependencies

claim: YouTube bot detection breaks downloads across all yt-dlp-based tools even when valid cookies are supplied, returning LOGIN_REQUIRED on every player client - a shared, upstream fragility affecting every candidate.
quote: even when users provide valid cookies via the --cookies flag, yt-dlp fails... YouTube's authentication system returns LOGIN_REQUIRED status across multiple player clients (TV, Android, web), forcing downloads to fail regardless of cookie validity.

claim: TubeSync users reported media stuck downloading and HTTP 403 Forbidden errors with downloads silently stalling starting January 2025, alongside reported database-locked and 'database unreachable' failures.
quote: Users have reported media stuck downloading with HTTP Error 403: Forbidden errors, and videos stopped downloading automatically starting in January 2025, with tasks showing "Downloading media" but never actually progressing.

claim: PinchFlat was front-paged on Hacker News as a self-hosted YouTube media manager built with Elixir, marking its emergence as the buzzed-about rising star versus the established TubeArchivist.
quote: Pinchflat: Self-hosted YouTube media manager built with Elixir | Hacker News
